summary: Backend-only test of Razorpay-simulated-signature purchase-to-email flow. All 3 pytest cases PASS (7.23s). (1) Single product 'ai-business-ideas-2026': create-order returned razorpay_order_id + key_id=rzp_live_TlI6IGn5mJOM2y; verify with HMAC-SHA256 signature returned {ok:true,status:paid,delivered:true}; GET /api/orders/{id} shows status=paid, delivery_status=sent, delivered_to=delivered@resend.dev, downloads[0].download_url returns HTTP 200. (2) Combo 'medical-6-pdf-combo' delivers exactly 6 downloads with delivery_status=sent. (3) Wrong signature returns 400 and order is marked status=payment_failed with no email dispatch. Backend logs confirm 2x POST https://integrations.emergentagent.com/api/v1/email/send -> 202 Accepted (one per successful verify) and zero sends for the bad-signature case. The expected Razorpay 'payment.fetch id does not exist' warning for the fake payment id is present and non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: email_service dispatch is awaited inside verify handler synchronously; if Emergent email proxy latency spikes, verify response time will grow. Consider BackgroundTasks for email dispatch so Razorpay-side callback acknowledgement stays snappy.
RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET is quoted in .env; current code strips quotes implicitly via dotenv — fine, but worth a comment to prevent accidental breakage.
test_credentials: none (buyer email delivered@resend.dev used as sanctioned test recipient)
seed_data_creation: Created 3 test orders in Mongo via live API (two paid + one payment_failed). Buyer email delivered@resend.dev.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To re-test purchase-to-email without charging real money: use HMAC-SHA256(RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET, '<razorpay_order_id>|<fake_payment_id>') and POST to /api/checkout/verify. Backend sends email via Emergent proxy and the httpx log line 'POST https://integrations.emergentagent.com/api/v1/email/send 202 Accepted' confirms dispatch. The Razorpay SDK warning about the fake pay_id is expected and non-fatal.
